capitals.name: Gremi
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Gremi (1466-1664)'. The Gremi page: 'capital of the Kingdom of Kakheti in the 16th and 17th centuries'; the kings 'transferred their capital to Telavi in the mid-17th century'.

capitals.name: Telavi
capitals.note: Infobox lists Telavi with no dates; 'Archil made it his capital in place of Gremi which was ruined by the Iranian invasions' (no year). 1664 is the end of Gremi in the infobox; Telavi's coordinates are the modern town's.

correction.text: Kakheti as Cliopatria's first shape, carried back to 1466

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Kakheti in 1468; the infobox says 'Established: 1466'. The 1468 shape is carried back unchanged.

23,396 km2, one outline for all four Cliopatria shapes (bbox 44.50-47.23E, 40.87-42.76N: Kakheti with Hereti and the Alazani-Iori valleys). The page gives no area and no Hereti or Tusheti borders, so the size is unchecked. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1579-1676, which Cliopatria leaves empty (its Ottoman and Safavid rows probably cover it). The kingdom continued as a vassal: infobox 'Vassal state of Ottoman Empire: 1578-1612; Vassal state of Persia: 1612-1723' (and 1555-1578), with Teimuraz I from 1605 and Rostom installed as vali in 1648. The 1468 shape is kept; the page gives no territorial change in the 1579-1676 span. Direct Safavid rule from 1677 is a loss in the ledger.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1703-1705: '1677-1703: Direct Safavid rule. 1703: The House of Kakheti was reestablished.' Cliopatria's shape returns only in 1706; the 1706 shape is carried back to 1703.

23,396 km2 for 1706-1737. The page has the kingdom under Ottoman vassalage from 1723 (Konstantine converted to Islam) and 'Successive Ottoman and Iranian occupations' from 1724 to 1744; Cliopatria keeps the outline, and the ledger hatches it as occupied.

correction.text: Kakheti, unchanged, under Iranian occupation but still Teimuraz II's kingdom, 1738-1743

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1738-1743, a Cliopatria gap (its Afsharid row probably covers it). Kartli page footnote: Teimuraz II ruled Kakheti 1732-1744 and then Kartli 1744-1762; Kakheti page: occupations 1724-1744. The state is kept, as occupied land.

23,396 km2 for 1744-1761. In 1744 'Nader granted the kingship of Kartli to Teimuraz II' and Kakheti to his son Erekle II (ruler list: 'Heraclius II (last)', 1744-1762); they 'exploited the turmoil in Iran that followed Nader's assassination in 1747'. Father and son ruled the two kingdoms until Teimuraz's death on 8 January 1762. [Reviewer eu-19-e, 2026-10-31: note corrected; the draft had the grants reversed and one king for both kingdoms.]

23,396 km2 for the year 1762 only: 'Teimuraz died on January 8, and Erekle II succeeded him, uniting eastern Georgia'. The map should show the union from January 1762; the 1763 Cliopatria 'Kingdom of Georgia' row is the united state.

ledger.note: 1466: Kakheti becomes a kingdom under George VIII. Infobox: 'Established: 1466'; 'The kingdom emerged in 1466 from the division of Georgia, after George VIII was captured in 1465 and then ruled Kakheti as an anti-king until his death in 1476.' Kartli recognized its independence in 1490 (infobox) and Constantine II recognized Alexander I as its king.

ledger.note: 1513: Kartli conquers Kakheti for a time. Kartli page: 'In 1513, Kartli briefly conquered Kakheti, and in 1520 Levan restored Kakheti.' The Kakheti page does not mention either date.

region.text: Kakheti, 'the easternmost province of Georgia centered on the river valleys of Alazani and Iori'

ledger.note: 1520: Levan restores Kakheti. Kartli page: 'in 1520 Levan restored Kakheti.' The Kakheti page puts Levan's kingship after Ismail I's invasion of Kartli without a year ('A two-year war followed, and Kartli recognized Kakhetian independence'); the Kartli page dates Ismail's capture of Tbilisi to 1522 or 1524.

1648: Persia ousts Teimuraz I and sets Rostom over Kakheti. 'In 1648, Teimuraz was ousted, and Rostom was installed as vali.' Rostom had been appointed king/wali of Kartli in 1632 (Kartli page); this is a change of ruling house inside the state, which stays a Persian vassal.

c. 1664: the capital moves from Gremi to Telavi. Infobox: 'Gremi (1466-1664)'; Archil 'made [Telavi] his capital in place of Gremi which was ruined by the Iranian invasions'. The infobox gives 1664 as Gremi's last year; the page gives no year for the move.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1578-1590)
wars.outcome: By the treaty of 21 March 1590 the Safavids ceded 'Azerbaijan, Karabagh, Ganja, Dagestan and Qarajadagh, as well as parts of Georgia'. Kakheti's infobox has it an Ottoman vassal 1578-1612.
wars.note: The war page does not name Kakheti or give Georgian terms by kingdom; Kakheti is included because its page dates the Ottoman suzerainty to 1578-1612. No contest events.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618)
wars.outcome: Abbas I's armies captured Tbilisi and 'both Kartli and Kakheti became Safavid dependencies once again' (1603-1604 section); the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha of 20 November 1612 'secured the 1555 borders envisaged by the Peace of Amasya'. Kakheti page: Abbas I 'subjected Kakheti to repeated invasions in 1614' (also 1615, 1616).
wars.note: The invasions of 1614-1616 devastated Kakheti but the pages give no held ground; Kakheti stayed a Persian vassal 1612-1723.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages; Kakheti's northern (Tusheti, Pshavi), eastern (Shirvan, Dagestan) and Hereti limits are approximate and the pages give none.

notes: Page budget: up to 5, five opened. The Kakheti page gives no area, no Hereti, Saingilo, Kiziki or Tush transfers and no year for Levan's 1520 restoration (the Kartli page supplies 1513 and 1520). Cliopatria: one outline (23,396 km2) for 1468-1578, 1706-1737, 1744-1762; no shape for 1579-1705 or 1738-1743 (new keyframes keep the kingdom as a vassal, apart from the 1677-1703 direct Safavid rule, which is a loss and a gain); starts 1468 against the infobox's 1466. Vassalage for the suzerain dossiers (all from the Kakheti infobox): Persia 1555-1578, Ottoman Empire 1578-1612, Persia 1612-1723, Ottoman Empire 1723-1736, Persia 1736-1747; Kakheti's Alexander II pledged allegiance to Tsar Feodor I in 1589, 'never implemented'. Disagreement: the Kakheti page puts Levan's kingship after Ismail I's invasion (no year) while the Kartli page has 1520 and Ismail's capture of Tbilisi in 1522 or 1524. The 1648 'rename' event records a change of ruling house under Persian pressure; the schema has no event for a vali's installation. The 1736-1744 Iranian occupation is a bridging reading (confidence 1): the page says Persian vassalage 1736-1747 and occupations to 1744. The infobox successor 'Elisu Sultanate' has no land on the page: needs a dossier (not in Cliopatria) and a region decision. Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' row 1763-1802 is the Kartli-Kakheti union that follows.
